$comment: The authoritative source closure for the `@muse-code/sdk` publication
and, since #638 S6, the Python SDK publication it shares a mirror with.
Every path below is mirrored verbatim from this repository into the public
venue `meta-models/muse-code-sdk`. The TS paths keep their layout: a
closure path `clients/sdk-ts` here lands at `clients/sdk-ts` there, which
is why the SDK manifest's `repository.directory` is the same string on
both sides. The PYTHON paths land under the mirror's `python/` tree
instead — see `mirror.python_tree` below.
This file is the producer-side authority: a republish reads it to decide
what to carry. It is not a digest, a count, or a copy of anything the tree
derives — it is the list itself, and `clients/sdk-ts/test/sdk-source-closure.test.ts`
checks that every path in it still exists and is still explained;
`clients/sdk-py/tests/test_source_closure.py` checks the other direction,
that the Python tree a wheel build needs is all listed.
Adding a path is a deliberate act: the closure is published source, so
everything listed here is read by people outside this repository and is
subject to the external-audience posture.
BUILD and TYPECHECK are standalone; the full TEST run is NOT. Two shipped tests
spawn the Rust conformance host by design - spawn-handshake.test.ts and
muse-serve-child.test.ts both invoke cargo - and no path here carries a Rust
workspace, so in the mirror those arms fail at the spawn. There is deliberately
no scrub step to patch them on the far side, so the mirror's README states the
expected failures explicitly instead. Adding a host-unavailable skip to those
two tests upstream is the way to make the mirror's `npm test` green by
contract; that is open work tracked as issue 29106 in the producing
repository. Until then 'test standalone' is not a claim this manifest makes.
The Python tree has the same caveat: its spawn-path suites drive the same
conformance host, and clients/sdk-py's transcript suites read the shared
schema/msp tree, which the mirror carries at its TS-layout location.
The source-audience gate reads this same list via closureRoots() in
scripts/check-source-audience.mjs, so CI cannot scan a different set of paths
than the publish carries - see docs/sdk-source-publication-profile.md. The
mirror step does NOT yet resolve its file set here and fail closed; that is
tracked as issue 27393 in the producing repository and is the remaining
drift risk.

preserve_note: Prose, not a path list — the list itself deliberately lives on one side only.
The mirror holds hand-authored repository-meta files that have no upstream
counterpart — its README, LICENSE, .github/, .nojekyll and publish-anchor.json.
The authoritative list is `repo_meta.hand_authored` in the mirror's own
publish-anchor.json, not a second copy here. A republish that replaces the
tree wholesale deletes them silently and still reports success; preserve
python_tree: The Python SDK closure lands under the mirror's `python/` tree, not at
its verbatim layout (ADR 638 D6): `clients/msp-py` here lands at
`python/clients/msp-py` there, and likewise for every path noted below
as Python closure. Extending the bridge to carry these entries is the
owner one-timer named in that ADR; the mirror's publish-pypi.yml calls

path_notes.clients/msp-py: Python closure. The generated wire-types package (PyPI muse-code-msp): the source the wheel is built from, and the tree scripts/sdk-py-wheel-rows.py reads the required host version and schema fingerprint out of.
path_notes.clients/msp-ts: The generated wire-types package the SDK compiles against. Private and never published on its own; it is in the closure so the mirror can build.
path_notes.clients/py-dev-requirements.txt: Python closure. The exact-pinned dev lock: the mirror's publish gates build with the same setuptools and build the producing CI proved, or the wheels are not the wheels the gates passed.
path_notes.clients/sdk-cookbook: The validated cookbook harness and its recipes. Published source: the docs site links readers straight at these programs.
path_notes.clients/sdk-cookbook-py: Python closure. The Python cookbook twins the docs site links readers at, same reason as the TS cookbook.
path_notes.clients/sdk-py: Python closure. The facade package (PyPI muse-code-sdk) plus its tests and the committed published-wheels.json record the compatibility page renders. Only src/ reaches the wheel; the rest is closure source. Its transcript and spawn suites read the shared schema/msp tree and the Rust conformance host, which the mirror does not scope under python/ — the mirror README states the expected failures.
path_notes.clients/sdk-quickstart: The quickstart journey a reader runs first. Published source, same reason as the cookbook.
path_notes.clients/sdk-quickstart-py: Python closure. The Python quickstart journey, the first-acceptance program the docs teach.
path_notes.clients/sdk-ts: The SDK itself — the package `npm publish` ships, plus the QA harness and tests that prove it. Only `dist/src` reaches the tarball; the rest is closure source.
path_notes.package-lock.json: Pins the workspace install the mirror's `npm ci` performs. Without it a mirror build resolves different dependencies than this repository did.
path_notes.package.json: The workspace root. It declares the `clients/*` workspaces that make the mirrored tree installable as one unit.
path_notes.schema/msp/msp.d.ts: The generated MSP declarations the wire types re-export. The SDK tarball bundles a copy at publish time; the mirror needs the source.
path_notes.schema/msp/stable: The stable schema bundle the conformance oracle and the wire taps validate against; the Python per-wheel rows read its manifest's fingerprint.
path_notes.schema/msp/transcripts: The recorded wire transcripts the QA harness replays, so a mirror checkout can run the conformance arm offline.
path_notes.scripts/check-msp-ts-typecheck.sh: The typecheck gate `clients/msp-ts` runs, which resolves paths relative to the closure layout.
path_notes.scripts/check-sdk-py-external-audience.p: Python closure. The external-audience gate over the built distributions (METADATA + packaged module docstrings); called by publish-sdk-pypi.sh, so it must travel with it — a republish without it dead-ends the Python publish at the audience gate.
path_notes.scripts/publish-sdk-npm.sh: Every publish gate lives here, and the mirror's `publish-npm.yml` is a thin caller that invokes it by path. If a republish drops this file the publish workflow dead-ends before it reaches npm — the workflow says so in one line and names this manifest as the place it must be listed.
path_notes.scripts/publish-sdk-pypi.sh: Python closure. Every PyPI publish gate lives here (the publish-sdk-npm.sh pattern); the mirror's publish-pypi.yml is a thin caller that invokes it by path, and its upload step runs only after this exits 0. A republish without it dead-ends the Python publish.
path_notes.scripts/sdk-py-wheel-rows.py: Python closure. Derives the per-wheel compatibility rows the publish gate requires and the docs render; called by publish-sdk-pypi.sh, so it must travel with it.
path_notes.scripts/sdk-source-closure.json: The closure carries its own definition: `clients/sdk-ts` is mirrored whole, including `test/sdk-source-closure.test.ts`, which reads this manifest at module load — a mirror without it crashes that guard with ENOENT before any arm runs.
